items.title: When the subscription's share runs out mid-run, the task gets a budget pause until the 1st instead of the stop the person's credential policy says (CE-6 was not built)
items.what_the_person_sees: The Claude subscription is first. When Forerunner's share of the subscription's allowance runs out during a task, the task pauses with a budget card that waits until the 1st of next month. This happens whatever the person chose under Settings, Which Claude does the work. Under 'then API key' the work does not go on with the key. Under 'ask before API key' no ask card comes. Under 'then wait' the person's session does not go on by itself when the month starts. Raising the allowance does not end the pause, and the change line does not say what happens next.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1880-1891: a refusal at level 'plan' becomes a paused handoff with source 'plan'. packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:233 and :266, and packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:158, :493-502, :574 and :700: the 'plan' card and its wake at the month's start. No money passes the share today, because the router holds the share at every new pick (packages/billing/src/router.ts:283-291).
items.fix_sketch:
1. In the executor's budget-stop branch, return a refusal at level 'plan' as a credential stop, the way the usage-limit branch does: reason 'share', a stopKey from stopKeyOf, and until set to the next month's start (UTC).
2. The task is given back with its kept work: the work-in-progress commit, the 'Where the last run stopped' brief, and no attempt counted.
3. The runner's credential branch then applies the policy:
- 'next': go on at once on the API key, from the kept work.
- 'ask': file one ask card for this stop.
- 'wait': the session ends to wait. It goes on by itself at the month's start, or when quiet hours end if that is later (decisions 8, 21 and 22).
4. The allowance raise in Settings gets CE-6's change line. It says the person's waiting session goes on now, or that the tasks are ready for the next Start.
5. Remove the subscription-share path from the budget card. Keep it only for an old stored per-source limit, if that is still reachable. Use the share's Wait lines that already exist in askCardWords.

items.title: When Claude Code refuses the sign-in, the task reads as Failed, not as a refusal: the Agent SDK throws after its error result, both consumers' catch blocks drop what they saw, and the synthetic error message is booked as a model
items.what_the_person_sees:
The person presses Start with an expired or invalid Claude sign-in. What follows:
- The task becomes Failed. Its card reads '"Write notes/pond.md" failed' / 'What failed: The run failed: Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.' with Try again, Mark done anyway and Cancel task. An urgent '... failed' notification goes out.
- Settings still reads 'Claude subscription · Does the work · Works now'.
- Chat answers 'I could not answer (model call failed).' On the bench it answered 'I ran out of time before I could answer.'
- Planning reads 'Planning failed: Claude did not answer (model call failed).'
- Every later call goes to the refused subscription again, and under 'then API key' nothing moves to the key.
- Costs lists a model '<synthetic> · 1 · — · — · CHF 0.00'.

API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."}'. limits.subscription has no refusedAt. Proxy ids 3-6 are chat's four 401s after the run's refusal. Files: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22/daemon.log, /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22-evidence/c22.json, /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22-proxy/requests.jsonl, and the screenshots /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22/steps/09-c22-inbox-after-refusal.png, 11-c22-settings-after-refusal.png and 12-c22-chat-question.png. C5:C5L-9 is a test gap: no composed case where a task run and a chat call meet the refusal at the same moment.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:572-581: the iterator throws after the result. The catch at :606-626 then overwrites `error` with code 'internal', so the mapping at :583-605 (usage limit, then authentication_failed) never runs, and the provider_auth that the result handler set at :482-490 is lost. packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:195-206: the catch yields provider_error, so errorFromSdk at :182-186 is skipped (sdkError and rejected are local to the try). packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:424-432: Claude Code's synthetic error message (model '<synthetic>', usage all zero) is booked and counted as a step. packages/runtime/src/provider/usage-limit.ts:123: REFUSED_TEXT does not match 'Authentication error ·'. The test fakes end the stream normally: cred-world.ts refusedReply, subscription-path.test.ts:520-535, claude-code-provider.test.ts:156-163 and sdk-driver.test.ts:342-346. Downstream: executor.ts:1755-1759 and routed.ts:287 act only on provider_auth.
items.fix_sketch:
1. Each consumer reaches one verdict about the stream, and it is applied whether the stream ends normally or throws.
2. In sdk.ts:
- Wrap the race on iterator.next() in its own try. When it rejects after the stream already reported a failure (sdkError set, or an is_error result seen), fall through to the existing mapping instead of the outer catch.
- Never overwrite an `error` the result handler already set (provider_auth, budget_exceeded for error_max_budget_usd, the usage limit).
- When the throw comes with no such message, strip the prefix 'Claude Code returned an error result: ' and classify the text with isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, text) and the usage-limit text check. A bare 401 in a run's own output still does not count.
3. In claude-code.ts: move sdkError, rejected and failure above the try. In the catch, yield errorFromSdk(...) or failure when one of them is set, and map the thrown text the same way. Keep the token cut out of the text.
4. Claude Code's synthetic error message (msg.error set, or model '<synthetic>' as one named constant) is not a model call: it is not booked, adds nothing to numTurns and gets no beforeModelCall estimate. If its usage is ever above zero, book it under req.model. Map a '<synthetic>' key in modelUsage to the run's model.
5. Change the fakes to the shape of SDK 0.3.304: a throw after the result, and the error message with model '<synthetic>' and zero usage.
6. Add one contract test that runs the real SDK against a local 401 stand-in, so the next SDK bump cannot bring this back. It skips with a visible reason when the Claude Code binary is missing.
7. Check the siblings the same throw hides: Claude Code's billing_error and rate_limit (CE-5's usage limit: the task rests, it does not fail) and error_max_budget_usd (a budget stop, not Failed).
items.test_boundary:
A composed cred-world test at the daemon's routes. Setup: both credentials saved, policy 'Subscription first, then wait', one ready task. The scripted Claude Code yields init, the assistant error (authentication_failed, 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.', model '<synthetic>', zero usage) and the is_error result, then throws Error('Claude Code returned an error result: ...').
Press Start with POST /sessions as the dialog sends it. Expect:
- GET /inbox holds exactly one card, 'The sign-in has expired or was signed out. Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits.', and no failed-task card.
- No '... failed' notification.
- The task waits; it is not Failed.
- limits.subscription.refusedAt is set, and GET /settings/credential-policy shows the subscription as refused.
- A following POST /chat gets the hold reply, and the scripted query's call count stays the same.
- GET /projects/:id/costs has no '<synthetic>' label, and no cost_ledger row has that model.
Repeat with the rate_limit error after the throw: the task rests until the reset (not Failed). Repeat with error_max_budget_usd: budget_exceeded.
Unit companions: ClaudeCodeProvider.stream yields provider_auth, and SdkAgentDriver.run returns provider_auth, both with the throwing fake.
C5L-9: a task run and a chat question meet the refusal in the same tick. Expect one refusedAt, one card, and no second request.
items.notes: Three findings merged: live4:L4-creds-9 (bench, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE contaminated) and live4:L4-creds-10 (real API, clean environment) are the same defect, and live4:L4-creds-17 is the synthetic message that defect reads wrongly. LC-C22 is the step that found it. The verdict rates L4-creds-9 major, against the finding's minor. It is the contributing cause of item L4-creds-4 (chat's 'Answered with ...' under a failure) and of LC-C26's Failed task. It also explains why every 'goes on with the subscription' step failed on the bench (LC-C24's continuation, LC-C31). Owner checklist: LC-C22 after the fix, plus a real usage limit mid-run (see owner_checklist).

items.title: Notifications about credential cards are built without the Inbox's context and are told twice: the reset time in UTC, 'Answer it in the Inbox' on a card with nothing to answer, a wrong reason for the refusal, doubled counts and pointers, and times that use the zone and clock the daemon had when it started
items.what_the_person_sees:
(a) The person's zone is Europe/Zurich. The urgent notification reads 'Use your API key until 07:26?' / 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 07:26. ...', while the card, the rows, the bar and Settings say 08:26. The second stop gives 07:01 against 08:01. So an urgent money question shows a reset that reads as already past.
(b) A refused key gives two notifications. The first reads 'Anthropic refused your API key' / '... until then the work waits. Answer it in the Inbox.', but the card has nothing to answer: its only action is 'Save a new key'. The notification says 'Anthropic did not accept it' where the card says 'The key is not valid or was deleted'. The second reads 'Field notes: Waits for a new API key: save one in…' / 'CHF 0.00. Open the session for the details.' An Inbox Update repeats the card as well.
(c) Notification titles such as 'Quote page: did 4 tasks: "Build the…" and 2 more and 1 more'. A session_ended body 'The card is in the Inbox. 1 task waits on other tasks. CHF 0.00. Answer it in the Inbox.' arrives 9 ms after the ask card's own urgent notification.
(d) Until the daemon restarts, chat's hold reply and its one-off offer keep the time zone, and the month cap's room, that the daemon had when it started.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:186-200: requestOpened calls requestWords(req, {projectName, taskTitle}) with no credentialAsk or credentialRefused context, and it always adds 'Answer it in the Inbox.' and the link /inbox. packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3434-3452: the humanRequest insert hook passes only the names. packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:1393-1394: askCard passes no timezone, and nowMs falls back to Date.now(). packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:231: validZone(undefined) returns 'UTC'. producers.ts:124-145: fit() rebuilds the quoted list but keeps the old ' and N more' tail. producers.ts:321-329: sessionEnded adds 'Answer it in the Inbox.' to a body that already points there. packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3812-3824 and :3986-3990: `told` is the project's open cards only, so the refused card (project_id null) and the ask card's wait line are not counted. packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:301-303: the 'credential wait' line is added with no check against an open card. compose.ts:5375-5428: credentialHold reads the composed `human` (timezone at :5378, monthly_cap_usd_micro at :5397). packages/billing/src/router.ts:223: `ctx.nowMs ?? Date.now()`.
items.fix_sketch:
1. requestOpened(req, humanId, names, ctx) takes the RequestWordsContext that the Inbox uses. Export views.ts credentialAskFor and credentialRefusedFor, or move them to a shared helper. The insert hook builds that context for CREDENTIAL_ASK_KEY and CREDENTIAL_REFUSED_KEY rows from a fresh read of the person, so the notification's title and body equal the card's.
2. A card with no choices, `reply: none` and one link does not say 'Answer it in the Inbox.'. It ends on its link's action ('Save a new key in Settings.'), and its link is the setup assistant.
3. askCardWords and stopWordsOf require the zone, so a person-facing sentence never falls back silently to UTC. askCard takes nowMs from the card's filed_at, never from Date.now().
4. fit(): when ' and N more' follows the list, add N to the count of names dropped and remove that tail, so one count remains.
5. sessionEnded points to the Inbox once.
6. Add ToldByCards.credential, set when the person has an open refused card or ask card for the stop that the session's wait names. The query is scoped to the person, not to the project. The 'credential wait' builder then leaves its line out of `news`: no session_ended and no Inbox Update for a session whose only news is that wait. The session page and the Overview keep the whole result.
7. credentialHold reads store.human.get(human.id) at each call.
8. RouteContext.nowMs becomes required, and every caller passes the clock.
9. Siblings: grep every caller of requestWords outside the Inbox (the email and Telegram channels reuse the Notification), and grep for Date.now() in the billing and credential code.
10. Update docs/maintainers/notifications.md ('Hearing once': the refused and ask cards speak for the credential wait).

The daemon log has 'merge record ... left_to_you head_moved' at 09:53:04.256Z, after the push's 200 at 09:53:01.691Z. items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:751-760: the head check reads the listing's head.sha (:756) and skips when it equals reviewed_head_sha (:757). packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:2094-2100: headMovedNow reads getPullRequest again, which lags the same way. 2. In headMovedNow, a getPullRequest head equal to the reviewed commit never overrides a newer branch head that was passed in. keepsOwnChange and the rebuilt-by-Forerunner case still decide as they do today.

decisions: One verdict per Agent SDK stream, whether it ends normally or throws: a refusal is provider_auth (refused, one card, the task waits), a usage limit is the subscription's rest, and an error_max_budget_usd is a budget stop. A bare 401 in a run's own output still does not count. Claude Code's synthetic error message is not a model call.

The subscription's share reached mid-run is a credential stop like a usage limit: reason share, until the month's start (UTC), named in the person's zone or the end of quiet hours. Under next the work goes on on the key from its kept work; under ask, one card; under wait, the person's session goes on by itself at the month's start (decisions 8, 21 and 22). The plan-level budget card is no longer used for the share.

A notification about a card says what the card's own view says, built from the same context as the Inbox, in the person's zone read at that moment. A card with nothing to answer points at its one action. A session whose only news is a credential wait that an open card already tells sends nothing of its own (design §4.3, §5.10).

Chat names the credential that answered only under an answer that was really given, once per stop per conversation. A failure is one sentence per error code that says what to do. Chat's hold reply says what still works and what to do, and chat's start follows the Start dialog: refused where it refuses, kept for the reset where it keeps.

The person's time zone and the monthly cap are read at each use, never captured when the daemon starts. Time comes from the Clock (RouteContext.nowMs required; no Date.now() fallback in credential code).
A call is booked on the credential that served it, finished or cut off.
The configured Anthropic API address covers every call, subscription task runs included (only when it is not the default).
A waiting session queued behind another project's session is the next one on the running bar, and its own line says it goes on after that session.
